key_insight: t-GQCE couples classical lattice dynamics to quantum embedding models, with added ghost orbitals improving correlated-electron dynamics toward nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results.
engineering_relevance: The framework assigns noninteracting lattice propagation to classical computers and finite interacting models to quantum processors, exchanging only Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices.
method: Map time-dependent multi-orbital lattices into classical quasiparticles coupled to quantum embedding models.
Propagate embedding states with adaptive variational quantum dynamics, while remaining compatible with other quantum solvers.
Reduce noise using circuit compression, rotated-orbital measurements, post-selection, and mitigation.
evidence_signal: Hubbard-quench statevector tests used 8–16 qubits with infidelities below 5×10⁻⁴; reduced-noise simulations reached 0.01 accuracy for density matrices and double occupancy at 10⁵ shots per time step, with similar accuracy on the Quantinuum H2-Emulator.
watch_item: Larger demonstrations rely on simulation or emulation; the reported reduced-noise accuracy requires one-third of hardware-benchmarked error rates and substantial measurement sampling.
paper_title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
